plan: Eight new items, topics searched in all verbal banks first, plus S026-08 and S026-10 resubmitted with corrected passages: persistent/even-handed WIC, sea-turtle central idea, leaf-folding hypothesis, its, which-clause, 'Today, however,', glass-frog cause synthesis.

passages.title: Eleven prototypes
passages.text: Although her first designs failed every field test, the engineer remained ______, rebuilding and retesting the water filter eleven times over three years until it finally met the village council's standard.

passages.title: Weighing two readings
passages.text: Reviewers praised the historian's account of the 1848 uprising as ______: it lays out the strengths of both rival interpretations of the event before cautiously favoring one of them.

passages.title: Lights on the beach
passages.text: Newly hatched sea turtles find the ocean by heading toward the brightest part of the horizon, which on an undeveloped beach is usually the open sky above the water. Along developed coastlines, however, streetlights and lit windows can be brighter than the sea, and hatchlings may crawl inland, where many die. In response, a number of coastal towns now require residents to shield or turn off outdoor lights visible from the beach during nesting season.

passages.title: Folding leaves
passages.text: Botanist Lena Ortiz hypothesizes that a desert shrub folds its leaves in the hottest part of the day mainly to reduce the amount of water the leaves lose.

passages.title: A quieter motor
passages.text: After two years of development, the appliance maker announced that ______ new electric motor for washing machines runs about 40 percent more quietly than the model it replaces.

passages.title: An old crossing
passages.text: The Fennick River ferry carried passengers and freight for nearly a century before the county built a bridge at the same crossing in 1931, ______ remains in daily use and was widened in 1978.

passages.title: A field without a plow
passages.text: For generations, farmers in the region prepared their fields each spring by plowing the soil deeply. ______ a growing number now plant directly into the stubble of the previous crop, a practice that leaves the soil undisturbed and helps it hold water.

passages.title: Glass frogs
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Glass frogs live in the rainforests of Central and South America.
• Many have skin on their undersides so transparent that their hearts and other organs are visible.
• When glass frogs sleep, most of their red blood cells move into the liver.
• This makes the frogs about two to three times more transparent while they rest.

passages.title: Listening plants
passages.text: Some plants appear to respond to the vibrations made by insects feeding on them. ______ in one experiment, thale cress plants that had been exposed to recorded vibrations of caterpillars chewing produced more of a defensive chemical when caterpillars later fed on them than plants that had not been exposed to such vibrations did.

passages.title: Who has seen the wind?
passages.text: "Who Has Seen the Wind?" is an 1872 poem by Christina Rossetti. In the poem, the speaker suggests that the wind's presence can be known through its effects on the natural world.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: rebuilding and retesting the water filter eleven times over three years
candidates.explanation: Rebuilding and retesting eleven times despite failure shows persistence.

B.rationale: "Complacent" means self-satisfied; she kept working because she was not satisfied.

C.rationale: "Ambivalent" means having mixed feelings; nothing suggests she was undecided.

D.rationale: "Impulsive" means acting without thought; eleven careful rebuilds over three years are the opposite.

hints: What did the engineer keep doing after each failure?
candidates.remember: Let the details after the comma define the blank.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: lays out the strengths of both rival interpretations
candidates.explanation: An account that fairly presents both interpretations before cautiously choosing is "even-handed."

A.rationale: "Polemical" means aggressively one-sided, the opposite of weighing both sides.

B.rationale: "Cursory" means hasty and superficial; laying out both interpretations is careful work.

C.rationale: "Partisan" means strongly favoring one side from the start.

hints: Does the historian treat both sides fairly or favor one from the start?
candidates.remember: Check that the word fits every detail, including "cautiously."

candidates.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Sea turtles return to the beaches where they hatched to lay their own eggs.
choices.B: Artificial light can lead hatchlings away from the sea, prompting some towns to restrict it.
choices.C: Undeveloped beaches are darker than developed ones because they have no streets.
choices.D: Coastal towns have banned all outdoor lighting in order to protect wildlife.

candidates.evidence: streetlights and lit windows can be brighter than the sea
candidates.explanation: The text explains how hatchlings navigate, how artificial light misleads them, and how towns have responded; B covers all three.

A.rationale: The text does not discuss where adult turtles nest.

C.rationale: This is implied but is not the text's main point.

D.rationale: The towns require shielding or turning off beach-visible lights, and only in nesting season.

hints: What problem does the text describe, and what response?
candidates.remember: A main idea covers the whole text, not one detail.

candidates.subskill: Command of evidence: textual (supporting a hypothesis)
candidates.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ortiz's hypothesis?

choices.A: Shrubs fold their leaves at midday even on cool, cloudy days with little sun.
choices.B: Folded leaves are harder to see for the insects that feed on the shrub.
choices.C: Shrubs whose leaves were held open at midday lost more water than normal shrubs.
choices.D: Shrubs near a stream fold their leaves as often as shrubs on dry slopes do.

candidates.evidence: folds its leaves in the hottest part of the day mainly to reduce the amount of water the leaves lose
candidates.explanation: If preventing folding increases water loss, folding must reduce water loss, which directly supports the hypothesis.

A.rationale: Folding on cool days, when water loss is low, would not support a water-saving purpose.

B.rationale: This suggests a different purpose for folding.

D.rationale: If folding saves water, shrubs with plenty of water might fold less; equal folding does not support the hypothesis.

hints: What result would show that folding saves water?

strategy.explanation: Predict an experiment that tests the hypothesis.

candidates.remember: Support for a hypothesis about a purpose often comes from blocking the behavior.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.explanation: The motor belongs to the appliance maker, so the singular possessive "its" is needed.

B.rationale: "It's" means "it is," which does not fit before "new electric motor."

D.rationale: "Their" is plural, but "the appliance maker" is singular.

strategy.explanation: Replace each choice with "it is" or "the company's."

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: remains in daily use and was widened in 1978
candidates.explanation: "Which" begins a nonessential clause describing "a bridge" after the comma; "it" and "this" create comma splices, and "that" is not used after a comma.

A.rationale: "It" makes a second independent clause joined by only a comma, a comma splice.

B.rationale: "That" introduces an essential clause and is not used after a comma to add a nonessential one.

hints: What noun does the final part of the sentence describe?

strategy.explanation: Rule out choices that make a comma splice.

candidates.remember: After a comma, "which" can attach a clause about the noun just before it.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.evidence: For generations, farmers in the region prepared their fields
candidates.explanation: The text contrasts a long tradition (plowing) with a current alternative (planting into stubble), so "Today, however," fits.

A.rationale: Planting into stubble is not an example of plowing.

C.rationale: The new practice is the opposite of plowing, not similar to it.

D.rationale: Plowing for generations did not cause farmers to stop plowing.

hints: Is the new practice like the old one or different?

strategy.explanation: Predict a contrast between past and present.

candidates.stem: The student wants to explain why glass frogs become more transparent while they sleep. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Glass frogs, found in Central and South American rainforests, are known for clear skin.
choices.B: Many glass frogs have skin so transparent that their hearts can be seen from below.
choices.C: Glass frogs become two to three times more transparent while they are sleeping.
choices.D: Sleeping glass frogs move most red blood cells into the liver, becoming more transparent.

candidates.evidence: most of their red blood cells move into the liver
candidates.explanation: Only D gives the cause (red blood cells moving into the liver) together with the effect (greater transparency).

A.rationale: This describes the frogs but does not explain the change during sleep.

B.rationale: This describes their normal transparency, not why it increases.

C.rationale: This states the effect but not its cause.

hints: Which note gives the reason for the change?

strategy.explanation: The goal asks for a cause; find it in the notes.

candidates.remember: An explanation must include the cause, not just the effect.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.evidence: Some plants appear to respond to the vibrations
candidates.explanation: The second sentence gives a specific case of the general claim in the first, so "For instance" fits.

B.rationale: The experiment supports the first sentence rather than contrasting with it.

C.rationale: "Nevertheless" signals something that happens despite the previous point.

D.rationale: Nothing in the second sentence contrasts with the first.

hints: Is the second sentence an example, a contrast, or a result?
candidates.remember: Specific cases of a general claim take "for instance."
candidates.revision_note: S026-08 resubmitted: the passage now says the plants were exposed to recorded chewing vibrations rather than sounds, matching the actual experiment, as a blind solver noted.

candidates.stem: Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.B: "But when the leaves hang trembling, / The wind is passing through."
choices.D: "Who has seen the wind? / Neither I nor you:"

candidates.evidence: can be known through its effects on the natural world
candidates.explanation: The trembling leaves are an effect on the natural world that reveals the wind's presence; the other choices only ask or state that no one has seen the wind.

A.rationale: The question alone does not show how the wind can be known.

C.rationale: This says no one has seen the wind but not how it can be known.

D.rationale: This shows that the wind is unseen but not that it is known through its effects.

hints: Which line shows something the wind does to something else?

strategy.explanation: The claim has two parts: unseen, and known by effects.

candidates.remember: A quotation must illustrate the whole claim, not just part of it.
candidates.revision_note: S026-10 resubmitted: the claim now concerns only knowing the wind through its effects, so the choices that show the wind is unseen no longer partly support it (a blind solver judged D partly defensible under the old two-part claim). Relabelled easy.
